en.name: Buckwheat, whole grain
en.summary: Whole buckwheat groats are not a wheat at all but the seed of a knotweed, and they carry a notably oily germ. That gives them one of the shortest cupboard lives of any grain: about 2 months sealed in a cool cupboard, and 4 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).
en.pantry: Keep buckwheat airtight in a cool, dark, dry cupboard and use it within about 2 months. That is genuinely short, and it catches people out — a bag of hard dry seeds looks like it should last a year. The reason is the oil in the germ, which turns rancid quickly and takes the flavour with it; rancid buckwheat tastes bitter and faintly soapy and is the usual explanation for someone deciding they do not like buckwheat. Buy small bags, keep them away from the stove, and smell the grain before you cook it.
en.fridge: There is no published refrigerator figure for buckwheat, so none is given here. Cold does slow the oil turning, so an airtight jar in the fridge is a sensible place for an opened bag in a warm kitchen — but the seal has to be real, because buckwheat picks up smells, and a jar brought straight out into a humid kitchen collects condensation. Let it warm up before you open it.
en.freezer: The freezer roughly doubles it: about 4 months at −18 °C (0 °F) in an airtight container or a heavy bag with the air pressed out. This is the right answer for a bulk bag, and it deals with pantry insects at the same time. Toasted groats — kasha — behave the same way, and freezing does nothing to reverse rancidity that has already started, so freeze it when you buy it rather than when you begin to wonder about it.
spoilage: A bitter, soapy or paint-like smell on opening — the classic rancid buckwheat.
A musty or damp smell, which means moisture has got in.
Webbing, small moths or fine dust in the jar.
Cooked groats that taste bitter however they are seasoned.
tips: Buy the smallest bag you can; two months is not long.
Freeze it on the day you buy it if the bag is large.
Smell before cooking — rancidity cannot be seen.
Buy toasted kasha if you use it rarely; the flavour masks age less well, but toasting makes the change easier to notice.

faq.a: About 2 months airtight in a cool, dark cupboard, or 4 months at −18 °C (0 °F).

faq.q: Why does buckwheat go off so quickly?
faq.a: Its germ is unusually oily, and that oil turns rancid faster than the starch goes anywhere.
Yes, about 4 months at −18 °C in an airtight container, and it settles any weevil question too.

zh.name: 蕎麥粒
zh.summary: 全粒蕎麥其實不是小麥，而是蓼科植物的種子，胚芽含油量特別高。這讓它成為櫥櫃壽命最短的穀物之一：密封放陰涼櫥櫃約 2 個月，−18 °C 冷凍 4 個月。
zh.pantry: 密封放陰涼、避光、乾燥的櫥櫃，約 2 個月內用完。這真的很短，也最常讓人措手不及——一包又硬又乾的種子，看起來應該可以放一年才對。原因在胚芽裡的油脂，它很快就會走油耗，並把風味一起帶走；走了油耗的蕎麥吃起來發苦、帶點肥皂味，而這通常就是有人「決定自己不喜歡蕎麥」的真正原因。請買小包、遠離爐火，下鍋前先聞一聞。
zh.fridge: 蕎麥沒有公布的冷藏數字，本頁也不給。低溫確實能延緩油脂變質，所以在溫暖的廚房裡，開封後裝密封罐放冰箱是合理的做法——但密封必須是真的密封，因為蕎麥很會吸味道，而罐子直接拿到潮濕的廚房會結露。開封前先讓它回溫。
zh.freezer: 冷凍大約讓時間加倍：−18 °C 下約 4 個月，裝密封容器或厚袋壓出空氣。大包裝就該這樣處理，而且同時解決櫥櫃害蟲。烘烤過的蕎麥（kasha）性質相同；冷凍無法逆轉已經開始的油耗，所以要凍就買回來當天凍，不要等到你開始懷疑它的時候才凍。
spoilage: 開封聞到苦味、肥皂味或油漆味——典型的蕎麥走油耗。
有潮霉味，代表濕氣跑進去了。
罐內有絲網、小蛾或細粉屑。
煮熟後不管怎麼調味都帶苦味。
tips: 買你買得到最小的包裝；兩個月並不長。
包裝大的話，買回來當天就冷凍。
煮之前先聞——油耗是看不見的。
很少吃的話可以買烘烤過的；香氣雖然蓋不住老化，但變化比較容易察覺。

faq.a: 密封、陰涼避光的櫥櫃約 2 個月，或 −18 °C 冷凍 4 個月。

faq.q: 蕎麥為什麼壞得這麼快？
faq.a: 它的胚芽特別油，而那些油脂走油耗的速度，遠比澱粉出問題來得快。
可以，−18 °C 下密封容器約 4 個月，還能順便解決米蟲問題。
